title: Legacy Application Insights: discovered, overlapping and cost savings tabs, application details, custom signatures and application tags

prose.label: Risk and compliance.
prose.text: {{risk-compliance-sections}} {{risk-attribute-answers}} {{risk-ssl-key-size}} The thumb for a key size of exactly 2048 bits is open {{gap:risk-ssl-key-size-2048}}.
Contracts are in [[business-insights.legacy.contracts]], the current All Applications UI is in [[business-insights.applications]], and the area hub is [[business-insights.legacy]].

discovered-apps-tab.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, The Discovered Apps tab charts the number of high- and low-usage applications and newly discovered applications for the last 12 months, and lists the top 10 discovered applications.

quotes: trend for the number of high- and low-usage applications, along with the number of newly discovered applications for the last 12 months.
View a list of the top 10 discovered applications.

data-source-values.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, The Data Source column names where usage was discovered: identity provider, ZIA, connector integration or custom application signature, shown as IDP, ZIA, CONNECTOR or CUSTOM ZIA, so one application tenant can appear several times; the Cost Savings tab's Data Source column names the source with IDP, ZIA or CONNECTOR as examples.

quotes: Data Source: The source from where the application usage is discovered (i.e., IdP, ZIA traffic, or connector integration such as IDP, ZIA, or CONNECTOR).

Data Source: The source from where the application usage is discovered (i.e., identity provider (IdP), Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA), by connector integration, or custom application signature such as IDP, ZIA, CONNECTOR, CUSTOM ZIA).
Hence, you might see multiple entries for the same application tenant with different Data Source values.

cost-estimates.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, Until costs are entered, applications show Zscaler-estimated Spend that is underlined, conservative (enterprise premium solutions with over 50% discounts, scaled by deployment size), and savings based on estimates are marked with an asterisk.

quotes: The Zscaler-estimated costs (Spend) are underlined. These estimates are conservative and take into account the premium solutions of the SaaS providers (i.e., enterprise) with over 50% discounts, and also take the deployment scale into consideration.
Cost savings for Zscaler-estimated costs are indicated with an asterisk (*).
By default, when you use the service initially, applications have an estimated cost populated for them until you enter or edit the costs for the apps.

cost-savings-tab.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, The Cost Savings tab lists the Top 50 Cost Savings Applications, where Cost Savings is the opportunity from removing inactive users, and plots a SaaS Efficiency Matrix by license usage percentage and expense with greater savings opportunities at the bottom right.

quotes: View a list Top 50 Cost Savings Applications.
Cost Savings: The cost-saving opportunity for the application by removing inactive users from the application.

View the SaaS Efficiency Matrix graph that shows the applications placement based on the license usage percentage and its expense to your organization, and indicates applications with greater savings opportunities in the bottom right of the graph.

overlapping-apps.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, The Overlapping Apps tab groups applications by capability, and Overlapping Users counts users using at least one of the applications listed for the capability.

quotes: Overlapping Users: The number of overlapping users who are using at least one of the applications listed for the capability.

overlap-details.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, The Application Overlap Details page compares overlap metrics for up to 4 apps at a time and charts the weekly active user trend for each application.

quotes: You can compare the overlap metrics for up to 4 apps at a time
The User Activity graph shows the weekly active user trend for each application.

overlap-comparison-columns.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, The Application Comparison table shows the top 5 departments by app usage, Spend in US dollars and a Contract Date that is the date the app subscription ends.

quotes: Top 5 Departments: The top 5 departments by app usage.
Spend: The amount spent (in US Dollars) by the organization on the app subscription.
Contract Date: The date when the app subscription ends.

details-status-risk.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, The Application Details Status field shows whether the app is onboarded and, for connector-integrated apps, whether the API connection is valid or expired, and the Risk Index is configured in the ZIA Admin Portal.

quotes: For connector-integrated apps, the application connector's API connection is valid or expired.
Risk Index: The risk index assigned to the application. This setting for the app is configured in the ZIA Admin Portal.
Status: The connection status between Business Insights and the application (i.e., whether the application is onboarded to Business Insights or not).

details-delete-connect.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, The Delete and Connect options on Application Details are available for connector-supported apps only.

quotes: These options are available for connector-supported apps only.
The top-right of the page displays the Delete or Connect option based on whether the application is connected for Business Insights computation or not.

details-users-graph-table.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, The Application Details Users table filters by the last 30, 60 or 90 days (last month, 2 months or 3 months for the ZIA table), defaults to Active Users, shows the top 100 records by user activity and exports to CSV; the active vs. inactive graph filters by the last 30 days or 12 months.

quotes: Select the time frame for viewing the data from the last 30, 60, or 90 days (last month, 2 months, or 3 months for the ZIA table).
By default, Active Users is selected.
The table shows the top 100 records by user activity.
Click Export to download the data for the preceding filters into a CSV file.
You can filter this tab for information for the last 30 days or 12 months.

details-users-by-source.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, The Application Details Users table depends on the data source: ZIA discovered or CUSTOM ZIA apps add Total Bytes, Upload Bytes, Download Bytes and No. of Transactions, CONNECTOR apps add License Type, and IDP discovered apps have their own table.

quotes: For ZIA Discovered or CUSTOM ZIA Apps
Total Bytes: The total upload and download bytes by the user for the app.
No. of Transactions: The number of transactions by the user for the application.
For IDP Discovered Apps
For CONNECTOR Apps
License Type: The license type of the application that is assigned to the user.
Upload Bytes: The total upload bytes by the user.
Download Bytes: The total download bytes by the user.

details-m365-obfuscated.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, For Microsoft 365, the User field on Application Details shows obfuscated data by default, and showing usernames requires enabling the setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

quotes: If you're viewing application details for Microsoft 365, the User field shows obfuscated data by default. To view usernames, enable the setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

contracts-tab-filters.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, The Application Details Contracts table filters by range operators greater than, less than, between, ends with, equal to and not equal to.

quotes: The Contracts table shows the list of contracts your organization is subscribed to for the application.
Use the filter-based range icons for precise data filtration (i.e., greater than, less than, between, ends with, equal to, not equal to).

licensing-insights.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, The Licensing Insights License Usage Funnel shows Purchased Seats split by SKU, Assigned Seats (applicable only to connector-based data sources) and Active Users (Last 90 days), filterable by data source and switchable between Plans and Contract views.

quotes: Purchased Seats: The number of purchased seats for the application. The graph is split between different SKUs that you purchased for the application.

Assigned Seats: The number of seats assigned to users from the purchased seats. Hover over the bar to view the number of assigned seats for each SKU. This information is only applicable for connector-based datasource.
Active Users (Last 90 days): The number of active users for the assigned seats.
You can filter this graph based on the data sources from the Datasource drop-down menu, or switch it between Plans and Contract views.

risk-compliance-sections.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, The Risk & Compliance tab has Hosting Information and Security sections and company details (headquarters, employees, year incorporated, application category, description), where a green thumbs up marks the desirable answer and a red thumbs down the undesirable one.

quotes: The Risk & Compliance tab consists of the following sections:
Headquarter: The application company's headquarters location.
Year Incorporated: The year when the application company was incorporated.
Employees: The number of people employed in the application vendor company.
Application Category: The application category that the application is categorized under.
Description: A description of the application company.
# Hosting Information
# Security
A green thumbs up next to that answer means that this is the desirable answer. A red thumbs down means that this is not the desirable answer.

risk-attribute-answers.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, On the Risk & Compliance tab, Yes shows a thumbs down for Poor Terms of Service, Data Breaches in the Last 3 Years and File Sharing in Hosting Information, and for SSL Pinned, Evasive, Weak Cipher Support, Published CVE Vulnerability, Vulnerable to Heartbleed, Vulnerable to Poodle, Vulnerable to Logjam and Remote Access Screen Sharing in Security; Yes shows a thumbs up for Source IP Restrictions, MFA Support, Admin Audit Logs and Password Strength in Hosting Information, and for Data Encryption in Transit, HTTP Security Header Support, DNS CAA Policy, Valid SSL Certificate, Support for WAF, Vulnerability Disclosure Policy, Sender Policy Framework, DomainKeys Identified Mail, Domain-Based Message Authentication and Malware Scanning Content in Security.

quotes: - Poor Terms of Service - Yes = thumbs down - No = thumbs up - Data Breaches in the Last 3 Years - Yes = thumbs down - No = thumbs up
- Source IP Restrictions - Yes = thumbs up - No = thumbs down - MFA Support - Yes = thumbs up - No = thumbs down - Admin Audit Logs - Yes = thumbs up - No = thumbs down
- File Sharing - Yes = thumbs down - No = thumbs up - Password Strength - Yes = thumbs up - No = thumbs down
- SSL Pinned - Yes = thumbs down - No = thumbs up - Data Encryption in Transit - Yes = thumbs up - No = thumbs down - Evasive - Yes = thumbs down - No = thumbs up
- HTTP Security Header Support - Yes = thumbs up - No = thumbs down - DNS CAA Policy - Yes = thumbs up - No = thumbs down - Weak Cipher Support - Yes = thumbs down - No = thumbs up
- Valid SSL Certificate - Yes = thumbs up - No = thumbs down - Published CVE Vulnerability - Yes = thumbs down - No = thumbs up
- Vulnerable to Heartbleed - Yes = thumbs down - No = thumbs up - Vulnerable to Poodle - Yes = thumbs down - No = thumbs up - Vulnerable to Logjam - Yes = thumbs down - No = thumbs up
- Support for WAF - Yes = thumbs up - No = thumbs down - Remote Access Screen Sharing - Yes = thumbs down - No = thumbs up
- Vulnerability Disclosure Policy - Yes = thumbs up - No = thumbs down - Sender Policy Framework - Yes = thumbs up - No = thumbs down

- DomainKeys Identified Mail - Yes = thumbs up - No = thumbs down - Domain-Based Message Authentication - Yes = thumbs up - No = thumbs down - Malware Scanning Content - Yes = thumbs up - No = thumbs down

risk-ssl-key-size.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, In the Risk & Compliance Security section, an SSL certificate key size of less than 2048 bits shows a thumbs down and more than 2048 bits a thumbs up.

quotes: The Risk & Compliance tab consists of the following sections:
Security Information
Less than 2048 bits = thumbs down
More than 2048 bits = thumbs up

custom-signature-limits.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, You can configure 32 custom application signatures, each with one host and up to 10 URLs.

quotes: You can configure 32 custom application signatures.
You can only add one host for a custom application signature.
You can add up to 10 URLs.

custom-signature-ssl.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, Custom application signature metrics need SSL inspection of the traffic enabled; for example, without inspecting the traffic for the Miro application, metrics are not visible beyond the host www.miro.com.

quotes: SSL inspection of the requisite traffic must be enabled for viewing the metrics for the custom application signature.
metrics won't be visible for anything beyond the host, www.miro.com.

custom-signature-host.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, Prefixes such as https://, http://, ftp:// and sftp:// are removed automatically from a custom signature host.

quotes: Host: Enter the host of the application. For example, xyz.com, abc.ai, etc. Prefixes such as https://, http://, ftp://, sftp://, etc. are automatically removed if added.

custom-signature-associated-app.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, The Associated SaaS Application of a custom signature displays metadata for a known application and affects the Discovered Apps, Overlapping Apps and Cost Savings metrics.

quotes: Associated SaaS Application: Enter the name of the application for which the signature is created.
This also impacts the experience of the Discovered Apps, Overlapping Apps, and Cost Savings metrics.
This helps to display metadata if the application is known to the Business Insights service.

config-recommendation.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, Zscaler recommends configuring a SaaS application connector (which requires admin access to the app) for the supported apps, or creating custom application signatures to pull metrics from a specific URL of the application.

quotes: Zscaler recommends configuring a SaaS application connector (requires admin access to the app) for the supported apps, or creating custom application signatures to pull metrics from a specific URL of the application per your requirements.

signature-list-columns.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, The custom application signature list on the Configuration page (Application > Application Settings) shows, for each signature, Application, Associated SaaS Application, Signature and Description.

quotes: On the Configuration page (Application > Application Settings), you can do the following:
- Application: The name of the custom application signature.
- Associated SaaS Application: The name of the application for which the signature is created.
- Signature: The signature details.
- Description: Shows any description added to the signature.

app-tag-limits.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, Application tags allow at most 8 tag categories, each with at most 8 tags.

quotes: You can add a maximum of 8 tag categories, and each category can consist of 8 tags.

app-tag-single.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, When manually tagging applications, only one tag in a category can be linked to an application.

quotes: Note that only one tag in a category can be linked to an application.

app-tag-dynamic-criteria.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, Dynamic application tag criteria are Engagement Index, Active Users, ACV, Growth Trend, Capability and Sanction Status, with operators greater than, greater than or equal to, less than, less than or equal to, equal to, Is, Is not, Contains and Not Contains.

quotes: - Engagement Index - Active Users - ACV - Growth Trend - Capability - Sanction Status

Operator: Select an operator to set the threshold to satisfy the criteria as greater than (>), greater than or equal to (>=), less than (<), less than or equal to (<=), equal to (=), Is, Is not, Contains, or Not Contains.

onboarding-entry-points.statement: In the legacy Business Insights help, Add App at Application > Application Insights lists the connector-supported applications, and the Add icon on the All Applications page or the Top 10 Discovered Applications table is how to skip connector configuration for a connector-supported app.

quotes: Go to Application > Application Insights > Add App.
The page shows the list of applications for which the Business Insights service supports connector integration.

If you want to skip the connector configuration for a connector-supported app and set up a ZIA or IdP gathered insights mechanism, click the Add icon for the application from the All Applications page or the Top 10 Discovered Applications table.

risk-ssl-key-size-2048.title: Which thumb an SSL certificate key size of exactly 2048 bits shows
risk-ssl-key-size-2048.detail: The legacy details page gives the SSL Cert Key Size answers only as less than 2048 bits (thumbs down) and more than 2048 bits (thumbs up); a key size of exactly 2048 bits is not covered by either case.
